QF.id: IV Strategies Using Interest Rate Derivatives_30

question.text: What distinguishes a covered call strategy from a naked call writing strategy in the context of interest rate derivatives?

answer.text: In a covered call, the writer owns the underlying bond; in a naked call, the writer has no underlying position
A covered call has unlimited profit potential; a naked call has limited profit
A covered call requires no margin; a naked call requires margin
A covered call can only be written on government bonds; a naked call on any bond

explanation.text: The Logic: A covered call pairs a long underlying bond (or existing holding) with a short call (workbook pp. 180-181). A naked (uncovered) short call has no offsetting long underlying, so a sharp rise in price exposes the writer to unlimited loss (workbook p. 170). The Trap: Covered calls have LIMITED profit (capped at strike + premium - purchase cost), not unlimited. The naked-versus-covered distinction is about whether the underlying position is held, not about which bonds are permitted. Note: Currently traded GOI bond options are cash settled (workbook p. 238), so settlement does not involve physical delivery of the bond by the call writer.
